llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions align with its stated purpose (a cloud AI SDK accessed via a CELLCOG_API_KEY and Python); nothing requests unrelated credentials or installs hidden code.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Any‑to‑Any AI SDK) match the requested items: python3 and CELLCOG_API_KEY. The SDK examples, endpoints (cellcog.ai), and features shown are consistent with a cloud service client.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to reference absolute local files using <SHOW_FILE> tags so the service can ingest them. This is coherent for a multimodal cloud SDK, but it means the agent will be prompted to send local file contents to the remote CellCog service—users should avoid including sensitive local files unless intended.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is embedded; the doc suggests pip install cellcog if needed. As an instruction‑only skill, nothing is written to disk by the skill itself. If you choose to pip install the SDK, verify the package source (PyPI) before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CELLCOG_API_KEY is required, which is appropriate for a cloud SDK. No unrelated secrets, config paths, or multiple credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced always-on (always: false) and does not request elevated persistent privileges or modification of other skills/configs. It allows autonomous invocation (platform default) but that is not combined with other red flags.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally coherent: it is a Python client for the CellCog cloud service and only needs CELLCOG_API_KEY. Before installing or using it, verify the SDK package source (e.g., PyPI) and the vendor homepage, create a scoped API key if possible, and be mindful when using <SHOW_FILE> tags—those prompts will cause local files to be sent to the CellCog service, so do not include secrets or sensitive files. Also monitor credit/billing usage since tasks can be expensive.
